newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swap - Naphtha moves into backwardation.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swap - Naphtha moves into backwardation.

text.p: Singapore naphtha swaps were firmly in backwardation at midday on Friday following a spate of physical purchases by a Thai petrochemical company which eased the physical overhang, traders said.
Traders said Thai Aromatics usually processes condensate for petrochemical production and the ongoing flurry of near-term naphtha purchases may indicate some technical trouble with their facilities.
As a result of the purchases, a 10-15 cents backwardation was established in the monthly time spreads over the three third quarter months.
July was quoted at $21.20/$21.20, August at $21.10/$21.30 and September at $21.00/$21.20, brokers said.
Brokers said July traded late Thursday at $21.25, August at $21.20 and September at $21.12.
Traders said the strength was also due to increased ethylene production in Japan.

Japan's ethylene output in June jumped by 10 percent from a year ago to 604,000 tonnes, and production for the first half of 1997 totalled 3.7 million tonnes, an increase of 5.9 percent from the same period a year ago.
Production was raised on healthy demand for ethylene-derived petrochemical products from East and Southeast Asian countries.
The gas oil swaps were steady but is still seen weak due to the prompt physical surplus, traders said.
July swaps were last quoted at $19.90/$20.05 per barrel up about 10 cents from Thursday with one lot traded earlier in the day at $20.07, brokers said.
August was quoted at $20.90/$21.00 also up about 10 cents from Thursday.
The July/August time spread remains wide and was traded late Thursday at minus $1.05 from about 90 cents on Wednesday.
Fuel oil swaps edged down due to the overnight 26 cents drop in August Brent which closed at $17.96 per barrel, brokers said.
July was quoted at $99.00/$99.75, down from Thursday's $99.50/$100.25.
